$comment: Gemfall beat 1, The Spark. Story: docs/campaigns/gemfall.md Â§1. Wiring: docs/campaigns/gemfall-authoring.md. Must set on every path to every ending: exactly one motive_* (choice_why_north, which every path passes through) and exactly one of ember_sold / ember_kept (choice_ember, which every path passes through). The six motive votes each land on a short result scene (scene_motive_*) before the docks, so the vote is seen to matter at the table. No combat: the Exchange is people, prices and promises. Expansion: the prologue ends on a vote (what the party was doing on the docks that night), and each pick pays off later in the chapter: the lamps open Old Wick's path over the Long Bridge, the oranges buy the sailors' rumors, the sardine feeds the gull. Further episodes: the jammed Long Bridge, the Griffin Post (whose friends can vouch for the stone), the gull, Mrs. Tuft's provision barge, Mortar's goodbye (whose word gets you hired by Hesper), and the North Gate on the way out. Second pass: a selkie family arriving on the quay (help them, and they make room for you when the Empty Chair inn is full) and the full inn itself.
title: The City That Smelled Opportunity

objectives.label: Listened to the scholar everyone laughed at
Heard the rumors of all three roads north
Signed on as real caravan crew

facet_ember.name: The Ember Facet
facet_ember.text: A red stone, warm as toast, that fell from the sky into an Exchange gutter by your boot.

scene_prologue_realm.narration: This is the Realm of Red Sky. Far in the north stands Mount Red Sky, the biggest mountain anybody knows. Old maps call it the Source of the Gemfalls, and add, in much smaller writing, that it is only sleeping.

choices.label: Go on

scene_prologue_city.narration: Far in the south, where every road and river runs down to the sea, is the Exchange: a busy city of towers, bridges and docks, where travelers from all over the realm come to trade, swap news, and find adventure. Nobody is from here. That is rather the point of it.

choices.label: Go on

scene_prologue_party.narration: And this is you: a little band of adventurers who met on the docks this week. Nobody has called you heroes yet. You each came here for a reason of your own, and you have not quite told each other what it is. Tonight the harbor lamps are just coming on. So what is our party doing on the docks tonight? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Fishing off the end of the long pier
Helping a ship unload its oranges
Helping the old lamplighter light the lamps
Doing card tricks for the sailors

scene_prologue_party_prologue_begin.narration: You sit on the very end of the long pier with a fishing line each and one bucket. In an hour you catch an old boot, a smaller boot, and one silver sardine. You keep the sardine in a pocket for later, because you never know. A seagull on the next post watches the sardine. The sardine, as much as a sardine can, watches the seagull.

choices.label: Keep fishing while the stars come out

scene_prologue_party_oranges.narration: A ship called the Sunny Disposition has come in packed to the mast with oranges. You pass crates down a long line of sailors until your arms smell like breakfast. "We owe you one," says the captain, a cheerful yeti with orange peel in his fur. "Sailors always pay their debts." He thinks about it. "Mostly in oranges."

choices.label: Sit on a crate and peel an orange

scene_prologue_party_lamps.narration: The lamplighter is a frogfolk called Old Wick, who is so old that his lamp-pole has a lamp-pole. You carry the ladder. He lights each lamp and wishes it goodnight by name. Then he shows you the lamplighters' path: a narrow ledge along the Long Bridge rail. "Nobody else uses it," he croaks. "Nobody else looks."

choices.label: Light the last lamp at the end of the harbor

scene_prologue_party_cards.narration: Your kitsune does card tricks on an upturned barrel. A sailor picks a card, and it turns up in his own boot. Then in his hat. Then in his sandwich. The sailors laugh so hard that one of them gives you his lucky stone, a smooth pebble with a hole in it. "You clearly don't need luck," he says, "so it'll be safe with you."

choices.label: Shuffle up for one more trick

scene_red_sky.narration: It is a quiet night at the Exchange, and then it isn't. Far to the north, the sky over Mount Red Sky turns red as a cherry, and a glittering rain of gem-light falls over the foothills. For one blink, some of it seems to fall up. A seagull drops its fish in surprise, and the fish looks surprised too.

choices.label: Fly up the lighthouse for a better look
Watch from the harbor wall
Run down to the docks and see what people do

scene_lighthouse.narration: From the top of the lighthouse the gem-light falls slow as snow. Then, just for a moment, one thread of it rises back toward the mountain, like a kite string being reeled in. The lighthouse keeper, a very old merfolk in a bathtub, says she did not see that. Neither did you. Officially.

choices.label: Glide back down and see what the city does

scene_harbour_wall.narration: From the harbor wall you watch the whole city find out at once. Every ship in the harbor swings on its anchor until its nose points north, as if the boats are thinking about it too. Bells ring on three towers, then stop, because nobody knows which ring this is. On the lighthouse, the great lamp goes dark for a moment, the way you might close your eyes rather than see something. Then it comes back on and pretends it did not.

choices.label: Watch the red fade, and see what the morning brings

scene_night_docks.narration: The docks are awake before the red has even faded. A boy on a ladder is already rubbing out the price of rope and writing a bigger one. A barrel on wheels rumbles past in the dark with a merfolk inside it, shouting "Rush prices, darlings, rush prices!" to nobody in particular yet. A yeti fishmonger looks north, looks at his herring, and quietly doubles the price of herring.

choices.label: Find a crate to sit on and watch it all begin

scene_stampede.narration: Three days later the Exchange is so full you can't see the cobbles. Merchants, scholars, pilgrims and pickpockets pour in from every road and every ship, all saying the same word: gems. The chalkboard prices change while you read them. A pie now costs as much as a tent, and a tent costs as much as a pony, and the pony has gone north with everybody else.

choices.label: Read the brass plaques on the harbor
Find somewhere to sit down and talk

scene_plaques.narration: Seventeen brass plaques stand around the harbor. Each one says who founded the Exchange, and each one names somebody different: a faun, a frogfolk, a family of selkies, and one that just says "my nan". Nobody is from here, so everybody is from here. A centaur tour guide says that is the best thing about the city, and charges you a copper for telling you.

choices.label: Find somewhere to sit down and talk

scene_long_bridge.narration: The best noodle stall in the Exchange is on the far side of the Long Bridge, and the Long Bridge is jammed. People are standing on other people's luggage. A goat is standing on a merchant, and the merchant is too busy shouting prices to notice. Nobody can go forward and nobody can go back. How do we get across?

choices.label: Squeeze through the crowd
Ride the cabbage barge under the bridge
Take Old Wick's lamplighters' path
Wade the canal beside the bridge

check_bridge_squeeze.prompt: Wriggle across a bridge where nobody can move

onSuccess.narration: You go sideways, then under a cart, then over a very patient yeti, and pop out of the far end like a cork from a bottle. The noodle stall is right there.

onFailure.narration: The crowd swallows you up and carries you the whole way across without your feet touching the ground once. It sets you down very politely, facing the wrong way, right beside the noodle stall.

scene_long_bridge_barge.narration: The cabbage barge is the only thing in the whole city that is still moving. The bargewoman lets you ride on top for a copper each, and charges the cabbages nothing. You glide under the bridge in the cool dark, past hundreds of dangling feet, and climb out by the noodle stall smelling very strongly of cabbage.

choices.label: Climb off and shake out the cabbage leaves

scene_long_bridge_lamp_path.narration: You find the narrow ledge along the bridge rail, right where Old Wick showed you. Nobody else is on it, because nobody else ever looks. You cross in single file, high above the whole jam. Halfway over, Old Wick himself is lighting a lamp at noon, just to be sure. He tips his hat as you pass.

choices.label: Hop down by the noodle stall

scene_long_bridge_wade.narration: Your bigfoot steps off the bank into the canal. It comes up to their knees. Everybody else climbs onto their shoulders, and then two strangers climb on too, and then the goat. You wade across like a walking tower, and the whole bridge cheers you all the way to the noodle stall.

choices.label: Set everybody down, goat last

choice_why_north.narration: At a noodle stall you find the one empty chair. Every table in the Exchange keeps one, for whoever arrives next, and today that is you. Everyone in the whole city is going north. So why is our party going north? Everybody vote.

choices.label: For the treasure. Gems, gems, gems!
To find out what really happened
So everyone will know our names
Because somebody has to keep folk safe
For a fresh start somewhere new
To prove we can do it

scene_motive_wealth.narration: "Gems," says Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall. He stirs the pot one whole slow turn before he says anything else. Then he chalks a new line on his board, RUSH PRICES, and your noodles cost twice what they did a minute ago. The crowd cheers you. Three pickpockets move one table closer. A merchant by the door writes your names down and underlines them.

choices.label: Go and find out what gems are fetching at the docks

scene_motive_curiosity.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, stops stirring, which he never does. "The gull," he says. "Dropped its fish before the light got here. Heard something first." He has clearly been thinking about this for three days. He tips your bowl so the soup slops into the shape of the mountain, and taps the top of it with one enormous finger.

choices.label: Go and ask the docks what they heard

scene_motive_prestige.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, turns round, very slowly, and writes your names on the specials board under TODAY'S HEROES. He spells one of them wrong. The whole stall applauds. A very small faun asks you to sign her dumpling, and you do, and she eats it straight away so nobody can steal it.

choices.label: Go where the news is made: the docks

scene_motive_duty.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, says nothing at all. He just fills a fourth bowl and sets it on your table. "For whoever needs it," he rumbles. The whoever turns out to be a faun at the next table whose field caravan left without her, and by the time she has finished the bowl she has told you every road north and which one her cousins are on. Then she spots her cousins' wagon going past, squeaks, and runs to catch it, waving her spoon.

choices.label: Wave her off and head down to the docks

scene_motive_fresh_start.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, reaches under your table with one slow hand and scratches three marks on the underside of the empty chair. "It's yours now," he says. "Everyone at the Exchange started over. Some of us twice." He gives you the heel of the bread for nothing, which at rush prices is practically a house.

choices.label: Take your first steps as new people: down to the docks

scene_motive_proving.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, points at a bowl on the top shelf that is the size of a bath. "Nobody finishes the Big Bowl," he says. You finish the Big Bowl. It takes all afternoon, and somebody has to be rolled off their chair at the end, but you finish it. "Hm," says Mortar, which from a stone troll is a round of applause.

choices.label: Waddle down to the docks, victorious

scene_newcomers.narration: On the way to the docks, a little boat bumps the quay, and off climbs a family of selkies: two grown-ups, a grandmother, and five children, carrying everything they own. They read the rush prices on the chalkboard and go very quiet. They came for a fresh start, in the same week as everybody else in the world. Just along the quay stand the harbor's brass plaques, the ones that say who founded the Exchange. Nobody stops to help. Everybody is busy going north.

choices.label: Carry their bags to the Empty Chair inn
Walk them along the brass plaques on the quay
Tell them we're starting fresh too

check_newcomers_carry.prompt: Carry a whole family's luggage up the busiest street in the realm

onSuccess.narration: Trunks, bundles, a rocking chair and a fishbowl with a very calm fish in it: you carry the lot up the hill without dropping a thing. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, and the five children wave from the window until you turn the corner.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up the hill the biggest trunk pops open, and out pour about a hundred knitted socks. All five children help you chase them down the street. It takes ages, and it is the most fun anybody has had all week. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, socks and all.

scene_newcomers_plaque.narration: You walk them to the seventeen brass plaques and find the one that names a family of selkies among the founders of the Exchange. The grandmother reads it twice. Then she sits down on her trunk and says, "Well, then. We're home." She unties a river charm from her own wrist and ties it to yours, "for the road north, since you're going."

choices.label: Wave goodbye and head for the docks

scene_newcomers_fresh.narration: "Us too," you tell them, and the whole family relaxes at once, like a sail when the wind drops. You swap the only fresh-start advice you know: eat at Mortar's, ignore the chalkboards, and save the empty chair for whoever comes next. They take a room at the Empty Chair inn and promise to save one for you.

choices.label: Head down to the docks

scene_docks.narration: The docks are where the Exchange trades its news. Here nobody asks where a thing came from, only where it is going. A boggart in a coat made of other coats is selling "slightly used rumors, hardly heard". A yeti fishmonger shouts the price of herring and, in between herrings, the price of roads.

choices.label: Swap rumors with the dock folk
Buy a rumor from the boggart
Read the crowd and hear what nobody says out loud
Find the orange ship's sailors. They owe us one

scene_docks_sailors.narration: The crew of the Sunny Disposition are mending sails on the quay, and they cheer when they see you. Sailors pay their debts, and they pay this one in rumors: one from every port they stopped at on the way in. The yeti captain throws in an orange each for the road, because he cannot help himself.

choices.label: Tally up everything you heard

check_rumours.prompt: Trade a good rumor for three better ones

onSuccess.narration: You trade the story about the seagull and the surprised fish, and the dock folk like it so much they pay you back three times over.

onFailure.narration: Nobody wants your rumor. In the end you trade your lunch for theirs, which is a fair price, because their rumors are better than your lunch.

scene_boggart.narration: The boggart's rumors come in little jars with the lids screwed on tight. You pay with a button. You open the jar, and the rumor inside is: "The mountain is grumpy." You already knew that. Then the boggart says it again, slower, looking sideways at the marsh road, and you realize it meant something else entirely.

choices.label: Take the jar to the dock folk and ask which road it meant

scene_three_rumours.narration: By sunset you have heard of three roads north. East, the queue at Stone Crossing is three days long, the trolls take a story instead of coins, and a river drake is charging double. Straight north, the old caravan road through the Plains is the shortest way, so everybody is on it, wheel to wheel. West, the frogfolk still pole travelers through the Whispering Marsh, if they like you, and the marsh has been noisy since the red night. "And mind the sky," adds the yeti. "The courier griffins are flying so overloaded with claim letters they can barely steer."

choices.label: Head back through the market, keeping one eye on the sky

scene_griffin_post.narration: On the way back you pass the Griffin Post, a tall tower full of round windows. Courier griffins queue on the roof while clerks stuff claim letters into their sacks, and then a few more, and then a few more after that. The postmaster, a griffin called Quill with spectacles on a chain, is losing count. "Hands!" she squawks. "Anybody with hands!"

choices.label: Help sort the letters
Share our supper with the tired couriers
Talk shop with the couriers

check_post_sort.prompt: Sort nine hundred claim letters before the griffins take off

onSuccess.narration: You sort them by mountain, then by valley, then by how loud the handwriting is. Postmaster Quill is so pleased she gives you a brave whistle, the kind couriers blow to clear the sky.

onFailure.narration: You sort the letters beautifully, into all the wrong sacks. A letter for a duke is now going to a duck. Quill sighs, says it will all come out in the wash, and stuffs everything into one enormous sack anyway.

scene_griffin_post_feed.narration: The couriers have been flying since the red night and have not stopped once for supper. You share yours. One young griffin eats a whole loaf in a single gulp, then a second loaf to check the first one was real. He bows to you with his wings out, which in griffin means: I will remember your faces.

choices.label: Wave them off into the sky

scene_griffin_post_shop.narration: Your griffin and the couriers talk wing to wing about headwinds, sack straps and the worst roofs to land on. Then they lower their voices. Since the red night, no courier will fly within a day of the mountain. "The air up there hums," says one, "like a kettle that's thinking about it." They make you an honorary courier, which mostly means free gossip.

choices.label: Swap one last bit of gossip

scene_gutter_glint.narration: Right on cue, a courier griffin wobbles overhead with a mail sack bigger than it is. The sack splits, and letters flutter down over the market like pigeons. Something heavier lands in the gutter beside your boot with a little plink. It is a red stone the size of a plum, glittering, and warm, like toast just out of the fire. It is also, very faintly, humming.

choices.label: Pick it up and pocket it
Shout "Whose is this?"
Call up to the courier who knows us

scene_gutter_glint_griffin.narration: The courier hears you, wobbles round, and lands on a chimney pot with his split sack in his beak. He peers at the red stone. "Not mine," he says. "That didn't come out of my sack. That came out of the sky, after it." He fluffs his feathers. "Finders keepers. Tell nobody I said so."

choices.label: Pocket it, and wave him off

scene_nobody_claims.narration: Eleven people say it is theirs. None of them can say what color it is. The griffin is already a dot over the sea, and the dot is not coming back. It seems the stone is yours, for now.

choices.label: Pocket it and head for somewhere warm

scene_gull_dive.narration: You have gone about ten steps when a seagull lands on the cobbles in front of you. It looks at your pocket. It looks at you. It looks like the very same gull that dropped its fish on the red night, and it has clearly been waiting three days for something better. Gulls love anything shiny. It crouches, ready to dive.

choices.label: Grab the gull before it grabs the stone
Offer it a bread roll instead
Throw it the sardine from the red night
Chase it off on the wing

check_gull_grab.prompt: Catch a seagull in mid-dive, gently

onSuccess.narration: You catch the gull in mid-dive, very gently, like a loaf of bread. It looks embarrassed. You set it down on a post, and it pretends that was where it was going all along.

onFailure.narration: The gull is quicker. It snatches the stone, flaps three circles over the market, finds it is much heavier than a fish, and drops it down the chimney of the nearest tavern. You run in after it and fish it out of the ashes, still warm, and only a little sooty.

scene_gull_dive_bread.narration: You hold out a bread roll. The gull considers the roll. It considers the stone. It takes the roll, and while you are feeling pleased with yourselves, it takes your other roll too. Fair is fair. It flaps away full and happy, and leaves the stone alone. Your tummies rumble all the way to the tavern.

choices.label: Go and find some supper

scene_gull_dive_sardine.narration: You pull out the silver sardine from the red night. It has had a long three days. The gull catches it in the air, swallows it whole, and from that moment on is your friend for life. It follows you all the way to the tavern door and waits outside, like a very small and very loud guard.

choices.label: Leave your new friend on guard

scene_gull_dive_outfly.narration: Wings snap open and up you go. The gull has never been chased by anything bigger than a cat. It flies one loop, sees who is behind it, and decides it had other plans today. A crowd on the quay claps. Two pickpockets who were also watching your pocket decide they had other plans too.

choices.label: Land with a bow by the tavern door

scene_tavern.narration: The Empty Chair tavern is packed with prospectors. On a table in the middle, a selkie scholar with ink on both elbows is waving her arms. "The gem-light fell upward! Only for a moment, but it did!" The whole room laughs, and two very polite stone trolls carry her out of the door, table and all. She keeps talking the whole way.

choices.label: Follow her outside
Tell her we saw it too!
Ask what it means. That is why we came, after all
Leave her be. There are gem-buyers to see

scene_scholar_believed.narration: The scholar stops wringing out her notes and stares at you. Then she hugs you, which is very wet, because she is a selkie and it is raining. "Professor Marrow Tidewell," she says, "and you are the first people who have believed me all week." She unpins the owl-feather clasp from her own coat and gives it to you, for clear thinking.

choices.label: Hear the whole theory

scene_scholar_theory.narration: Outside, the scholar draws on a napkin. Professor Tidewell, says the name on her soggy notes. The drawing is a shape with eight sides, like a gem cut by somebody very careful. "The oldest stories tell of a seal, like a lid on a jar, with eight great facets. I think the mountain just threw seven of them across the realm, and everybody is selling them. The eighth is still in the mountain." Then she looks at your pocket, which is glowing slightly. "Oh," she says. "You've got one."

choices.label: Thank her, and think about it

choice_ember.narration: Gem-buyers line the whole quay. The biggest is Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk who gets about in a barrel on wheels, and she smells your warm red stone from ten stalls away. "Rush prices, darlings," she says, and names a number so big that a pigeon faints. Do we sell it, or keep it?

choices.label: Sell it to Madame Fenn
Haggle her up even higher, then sell
Keep it

choice_ember_sell_high.narration: You name a bigger number. Madame Fenn names a smaller one. You name a bigger one again, and a second pigeon faints. In the end she pays twice what she offered, laughs so hard her barrel rolls into a bollard, and throws in a brave whistle "for cheek, darlings." Then she writes your names in her little green book, twice.

choices.label: Take the clanking purse

scene_sold.narration: Madame Fenn pays with a purse so heavy it clanks, and throws in a hearthstone bead "for luck, darlings." Then she writes your names in a little green book. "I never forget a good seller," she says, and somehow you believe her. The stone goes into her barrel, still humming, and the humming goes with it.

choices.label: Go and spend some of it

scene_kept.narration: You close your hand around the stone. Still warm. Madame Fenn sighs a sigh so big her barrel rocks on its wheels. "Your loss, darlings. Or somebody's." The stone feels a little heavier now, the way a promise does.

choices.label: Go and get ready for the road

scene_provisions.narration: First, food for the road. A provision barge is moored at the foot of the Outfitters' Steps, run by Mrs. Tuft, a sheeple grocer whose wool is stuck all over with price tags. Everything she sells comes in a jar, even the jars. There is room in the pack for one good thing. What shall it be?

choices.label: A tin of honeycakes, for sharing
A sunbloom draught, for bumps and scrapes
A jar of mosslight, for dark roads
Show Mrs. Tuft the warm red stone

scene_provisions_honey.narration: Mrs. Tuft packs six honeycakes into a tin, then a seventh "for the tin". You all promise to save them for the road. By the top of the Outfitters' Steps there are five. Nobody knows what happened to the other two, and everybody has crumbs on their chin.

choices.label: Climb the steps to the cobbler

scene_provisions_sunbloom.narration: The sunbloom draught glows in its bottle like a little sunrise. "For bumps, scrapes and grumps," says Mrs. Tuft. "Mostly grumps." She wraps it in a sock so it will not clink against anything, and then charges you for the sock.

choices.label: Climb the steps to the cobbler

scene_provisions_mosslight.narration: The mosslight glows soft and green, like a tiny forest that fits in your hand. "Picked far to the west by my cousins," says Mrs. Tuft. "It likes to be talked to. Not sung to. It's very particular." The jar seems to brighten a little when you say thank you.

choices.label: Climb the steps to the cobbler

scene_provisions_stone.narration: Mrs. Tuft takes one look at the red stone, and every jar on her barge starts to rattle on its shelf, very gently, the way spoons do when a cart goes by. She hands it back rather quickly. "Lovely," she says, not meaning it. She gives you a honeycake for free, and you get the feeling it is so you will leave a bit sooner.

choices.label: Pocket the stone and climb the steps

scene_market.narration: Every shop on the Outfitters' Steps is selling the same three things: boots, rope, and quickfoot laces. A faun cobbler called Tobble Reedpipe sings the price of each lace as he sells it, and every verse goes up a key. By the top of the steps he is squeaking.

choices.label: Haggle with Tobble
Buy the best laces outright. We're rich now!
Tell Tobble we're after a fresh start
Point out the fake laces on the next stall

scene_market_spot_fakes.narration: Your kitsune sniffs once and points. "Those are bootlaces painted yellow." The stall-keeper next door goes very red, packs up in about four seconds, and is never seen on the Outfitters' Steps again. Tobble is so grateful he presses real quickfoot laces on you and sings your names up the whole scale.

choices.label: Lace up

scene_market_fresh_start.narration: Tobble stops singing. "A fresh start," he says, and for once he just speaks. He has one too, he says. He used to make boots for a duke, and then he decided he liked laces better. He sells you the laces at last year's price and sings a small verse about beginnings that nearly rhymes.

choices.label: Lace up

scene_market_buy_outright.narration: You point at the best laces on the rack and pay without asking the price. Tobble is so startled he sings the price anyway, out of habit, a whole key too high. Three prospectors turn round to see who is rich. You try to look like you have always been rich.

choices.label: Lace up

check_haggle.prompt: Haggle with a cobbler who is singing the price

onSuccess.narration: You sing back, one key lower. Tobble is so delighted he sells you the laces at last week's price.

onFailure.narration: You haggle so hard that Tobble loses his place in the song and starts again from the top, twice. Somewhere in the muddle, money changes hands and something is wrapped in paper.

scene_laced.narration: The quickfoot laces go on, and right away your feet would like to be somewhere else, quickly. Tobble sings a little verse about you. It is very flattering and mostly does not rhyme.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

scene_lace_tangle.narration: You haggle so hard that Tobble gets muddled and sells you a honeycake instead of laces. You are not sure how that happened. Neither is Tobble. It is a very good honeycake, though.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

scene_inn_full.narration: Every inn in the Exchange is full to the chimneys. At the Empty Chair, Innkeeper Flint, a stone troll in a very small nightcap, has one bed left: a cupboard under the stairs. Four other groups of prospectors want it too. Flint folds his arms. "Best offer," he rumbles. How do we win the cupboard?

choices.label: Tell the best story of the red night
Offer to wash up the supper bowls for it
Find the selkie family upstairs
Outbid everybody with Madame Fenn's purse

check_inn_story.prompt: Tell the red night so well a whole inn goes quiet

onSuccess.narration: You tell it all: the cherry-red sky, the gem-light falling, the seagull and its very surprised fish. The whole inn goes quiet. Flint wipes one eye with a dishcloth and hands you the cupboard key without a word.

onFailure.narration: Your story wanders off somewhere around the fish and never quite comes back. The prospectors laugh so kindly that Flint gives the cupboard to someone else and you the hayloft above the mules, which is warm, smells of apples, and is honestly nicer.

scene_inn_full_dishes.narration: There are three hundred supper bowls, and some of them have been used twice. You wash, dry and stack until your fingers go wrinkly as raisins and the kitchen is full of soap bubbles. At midnight Flint inspects one bowl very closely, says "Hm," and hands you the key. The other prospectors are still arguing about prices.

choices.label: Squeeze into the cupboard

scene_inn_full_selkies.narration: The selkie family you helped today hear your voices and come thundering down the stairs. "You'll squash in with us," says the grandmother, and that is the end of the argument. Their room is tiny, and eight selkies is a lot of selkie, but it is warm. The five children want a bedtime story, and they want it about you.

choices.label: Squash in and tell the story

scene_inn_full_outbid.narration: You open Madame Fenn's clanking purse and name a number. The other prospectors go pale and wander off to sleep in the stables. Flint bites one coin to check it is real, then another to check the first one was. The cupboard is yours. It is still a cupboard, but it is the most expensive cupboard in the realm.

choices.label: Admire your very expensive cupboard

rest_empty_chair.narration: Cupboard, hayloft or squashed-up room, it is warm and dry, and somebody shares out supper. Through the wall, three people in three languages argue happily about the price of onions, and all three of them are right. Tomorrow the caravans leave.

choices.label: Up at dawn for the caravan yard

scene_last_noodles.narration: On the way to the caravan yard you pass the noodle stall. Mortar is already up, or has never gone to bed. He looks at your packed bags. He stirs one whole slow turn. "Going, then," he says. The caravans are lighting their lanterns, but there is time for one thing before you go.

choices.label: Ask him which caravan to join
Leave a gift on the empty chair
Eat one last bowl, for the road
Let Mortar listen to the warm stone

scene_last_noodles_ask.narration: Mortar stirs one whole slow turn. Then another. "Longstride," he says at last. "Lantern wagon. Listens to the whole answer." He taps the table with one enormous finger. "Tell her Mortar sent you." That is more words than he has said all week, and he looks a bit tired afterwards.

choices.label: Thank him, and head for the lantern wagon

scene_last_noodles_gift.narration: Every table in the Exchange keeps an empty chair for whoever comes next. You leave a button on it, and a note that says GOOD LUCK in all your different handwritings. Underneath, tied to the chair leg, you find a songbird ribbon. Somebody left it there for you, before you ever came. Mortar pretends not to see. He is smiling, very slowly.

choices.label: Tie on the ribbon and go

scene_last_noodles_bowl.narration: Mortar ladles out the biggest breakfast of your lives. When you are done, he unpins the little thistle from his apron and pins it on you. "Strong noodles," he rumbles. "Strong legs." Then, after a long stir: "Come back." Two words, which from a stone troll is practically a speech.

choices.label: Wave goodbye with full tummies

scene_last_noodles_listen.narration: Mortar holds the warm stone to his great stone ear for a long, long time. The whole stall goes quiet. "Sings," he says at last. "Like my nan's pot, just before it boiled over." He gives it back to you very carefully, the way you hand somebody a baby bird, and fills your water flasks for nothing.

choices.label: Tuck the stone away and go

scene_caravan_yard.narration: At dawn the caravan yard is a sea of wagons, all pointed north. The one with the most lanterns belongs to Hesper Longstride, a centaur caravan master whose sash is stitched all over with roads. She looks your party up and down the way she looks at weather. "Room for one more crew," she says. "Why should it be you?"

choices.label: Tell her honestly why we're going
Lift the stuck wagon out of the mud
Offer to guard the lantern wagon
Bet we can load a wagon faster than anyone
Offer to carry the banner at the front
Tell Hesper that Mortar sent us

scene_caravan_yard_banner.narration: The banner is taller than any of you and heavier than it looks, and the wind off the harbor wants it very badly. You hold it up anyway. The whole yard turns to look at who is carrying the Longstride banner, and Hesper lets them look. "Front," she says. "Don't drop it."

choices.label: Take your place at the front

scene_caravan_yard_race.narration: A yeti crew bets you cannot load a wagon faster than they can. You load it in the time it takes them to argue about who goes first. Half of it is loaded upside down, but it is loaded. The yetis pay up in dried apples, and Hesper, very slightly, smiles.

choices.label: Collect your winnings

scene_caravan_yard_guard.narration: "The lantern wagon," says Hesper, "has been robbed twice this week and set on fire once." You say you will guard it anyway. She looks at you the way she looks at weather that has decided to be useful, and hands you a long pole with a hook on the end.

choices.label: Take up your post

scene_caravan_yard_lift_wagon.narration: You walk over to the wagon stuck in the mud, take hold of the back axle, and lift. The wagon comes up. So does the mud. So does a small faun who was sitting in the wagon eating breakfast, and who keeps eating it. Hesper watches the whole thing without a word, then nods once.

choices.label: Report for duty

scene_caravan_yard_mortar.narration: Hesper's ears turn right round. "Mortar," she says. "How many words did he say about you?" You count. Four. She is quiet for a moment, the way weather is quiet before it decides something. Then she nods once. From a stone troll, four words is a letter of recommendation.

choices.label: Report for duty

check_signon.prompt: Tell a caravan master the truth and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Hesper listens to the whole answer, all the way to the end. Then she nods once, like a gate closing.

onFailure.narration: You get muddled halfway through and say "um" eleven times. Hesper is kind about it. Hesper is also busy.

scene_hired.narration: Hesper hands you each a lantern pole. "Crew," she says, which on a caravan means you eat first and sleep last. The wagons begin to roll, and you roll with them, through the crowded streets to the North Gate, where everybody leaving the Exchange stops for one last thing.

choices.label: Roll north

scene_turnip_wagon.narration: "Cargo, then," says Hesper, kindly. You ride out squashed into a wagon full of turnips, which is not glamorous, but it is going north. One turnip rolls into your lap and stays there, like a cat. At the North Gate the wagons stop for one last thing.

choices.label: Roll north anyway

scene_north_gate.narration: The North Gate is where the city says goodbye. Over the arch hangs the Leaving Bell, with a rope worn smooth by a thousand travelers. Beyond it, the road runs out into the green fields, and far away on the edge of the world sits Mount Red Sky. Hesper gives you one minute. How do we leave the Exchange?

choices.label: Ring the Leaving Bell
Wave goodbye to everyone we met
Turn round and face the mountain
Look for Professor Tidewell in the crowd

check_leaving_bell.prompt: Ring the Leaving Bell loud enough for the whole city

onSuccess.narration: You haul on the rope together. BONG. The bell is so loud that every gull in the harbor lifts off at once, and all over the Exchange, people you have never met stop and wave you goodbye.

onFailure.narration: You haul on the rope, and the rope hauls back. Up you go, dangling under the bell like the world's most surprised clapper. It rings anyway. The whole gate cheers, and Hesper waits, very patiently, for you to come down.

scene_north_gate_wave.narration: You wave, and the Exchange waves back. Tobble sings a goodbye verse from the Outfitters' Steps, three keys too high. Madame Fenn's barrel rolls along the quay to keep up. "Bring me back something shiny, darlings!" High on the lighthouse, the great lamp winks twice, as if it knows something.

choices.label: Keep waving until the roofs are gone

scene_north_gate_look.narration: You turn your backs on the city and look north. Far away, over the fields, Mount Red Sky sits on the edge of the world with a little red glow on top, like a candle somebody forgot to blow out. For one blink you feel as if it is looking back. Then a wheel hits a bump, and it is just a mountain again.

choices.label: Keep your eyes on the road ahead

scene_north_gate_tidewell.narration: There she is, running alongside the wagons with an armful of soggy notes. "Count them!" shouts Professor Tidewell. "Every stone you see, count it! Write it down!" She throws you a napkin with an eight-sided shape drawn on it, trips over a goose, and keeps waving from the ground until you are out of sight.

choices.label: Fold up the napkin and keep it safe

rest_northbound.narration: That night the caravan camps in the first of the Sunward Fields, where the grass smells of honey and everybody's boots still smell of the city. Far to the north the sky glows faintly red, like a coal somebody forgot to put out. Share out your things, patch each other up, and get some sleep. The road starts properly tomorrow.

forbidden: any one people owning or founding the Exchange
explaining what the gemstones really are

npcVoices.tidewell: Professor Marrow Tidewell, a selkie scholar with ink on both elbows; talks fast, draws on napkins, has been laughed out of better taverns and keeps going anyway
npcVoices.coralie_fenn: Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; calls everyone darlings, names enormous numbers cheerfully, never forgets a seller
npcVoices.tobble: Tobble Reedpipe, a faun cobbler who sings every price, going up a key each verse; delighted by anyone who sings back
npcVoices.hesper: Hesper Longstride, a centaur caravan master with a road-stitched sash; few words, listens to the whole answer, kind but busy
npcVoices.boggart: a rumor-selling boggart in a coat made of other coats; never says anything straight, always says it twice
npcVoices.lighthouse_keeper: a very old merfolk in a bathtub at the top of the lighthouse; firmly did not see anything
npcVoices.tour_guide: a centaur tour guide who loves the seventeen plaques and charges for every fact
npcVoices.mortar: Mortar, a stone troll noodle cook; stirs one full slow turn before answering anything, says very little, and means all of it
npcVoices.old_wick: Old Wick, a very old frogfolk lamplighter; croaks softly, wishes every lamp goodnight by name, knows the paths nobody else looks for
npcVoices.orange_captain: the yeti captain of the Sunny Disposition, an orange ship; cheerful, orange peel in his fur, pays every debt, mostly in oranges
npcVoices.postmaster_quill: Postmaster Quill, a griffin with spectacles on a chain who runs the Griffin Post; squawks, loses count, insists it will all come out in the wash
npcVoices.courier_griffin: a young courier griffin, always hungry, bows with wings out to people it will remember
npcVoices.mrs_tuft: Mrs. Tuft, a sheeple grocer on a provision barge, wool full of price tags; everything comes in a jar; brisk and a little dry
npcVoices.selkie_grandmother: the grandmother of a selkie family just arrived for a fresh start; brisk, warm, decides things are settled and they are
npcVoices.innkeeper_flint: Innkeeper Flint, a stone troll who runs the Empty Chair inn in a very small nightcap; rumbles, folds his arms, secretly soft
